title: The hidden overloads
description:
`Printer` has two `show` functions. `FancyPrinter` adds a third, for text. That one new `show` **hides both of the inherited ones**: name lookup stops at the first class that has the name. As written, `fancy.show(5)` does not even compile.

Add one line to `FancyPrinter` to bring the inherited overloads back into view.
hints: `using Printer::show;` inside the derived class makes every base overload of that name visible alongside the new one.
unitTests:
TEST("the new overload") { CHECK_EQ(FancyPrinter{}.show(std::string_view{ "hi" }), "<<hi>>"); }
TEST("the inherited overloads are visible again") { const FancyPrinter f{}; CHECK_EQ(f.show(5), "int 5"); CHECK_EQ(f.show(true), "yes"); }

grading.unitTests:
